workload.note: internet egress only; same 500 GB as video #1

backblaze_b2.note: free egress up to 3x avg monthly stored data, then $0.01/GB

cloudflare_r2.note: zero egress to internet, Standard storage

_regulation.status: AWS, Azure and Google all already waive egress — but only for customers leaving.

methodology_notes: GCP is ABSENT: its egress table is JS-rendered and the public pricing endpoints are retired. Needs a (free) Cloud Billing API key. Do not estimate it.
Backblaze and Cloudflare 'free' is conditional: B2 is free to 3x stored data; R2 is free for Standard storage egress to internet.
DigitalOcean pools a per-Droplet allowance across the team; 500 GB sits inside a single Droplet's allowance.
Hetzner includes 20 TB, so 500 GB has zero marginal cost -- not merely cheap.
Object-store providers (R2, B2, Wasabi) are not substitutes for a compute VM's egress. Compared here on egress price only.
Wholesale transit converted to $/GB assuming a month of 730h. At 100% port utilisation 1 Mbps moves ~328 GB; real networks average far less, so the conservative figure assumes 50%.
AWS at-scale figures use the published tier breaks (100 GB free, then $0.09 / $0.085 / $0.07 / $0.05).
The markup compares a retail per-GB price to a wholesale port price. They are different products -- the comparison bounds the input cost, it is not a margin calculation.

sources.wholesale_transit: TeleGeography IP Transit Pricing, Q2 2026 weighted median 100 GigE US/EU (2026-10-27)
sources.eu_data_act: EU Data Act Chapter 6; hyperscaler egress-waiver programmes (2026-10-27)
